sentences.text: Petitioners have filed the petition U/sec.166 of Motor Vehicle Act, 1988, claiming compensation amount of Rs.2,00,00,000/- with interest from the respondents.

2. Petitioners case is as Follows:
Petitioner no.1 and 2 are the parents of the deceased Monish.K.

That on 21.01.2024 at about 02.30 AM., Dasari Monish.K was moving in motor cycle bearing No.KA-03- JQ-2422, near B Channasandra skywalk, Ramamurthynagar, ring road, Bangalore,
wherein the driver of the Lorry bearing Reg No.KA-53-D-6152 drove it, with high speed rash and negligent manner dashed against deceased vehicle.

Due to the impact,
deceased was fell down, lorry wheel ran over the deceased and died due to the accidental injuries on the same in the hospital.
He was shifted to Manipal hospital and he died due to the accidental injuries.
Autopsy was conducted at East Point hospital.
The petitioners have performed funeral and obsequies as per their customs and they have spent more than Rs.1,00,000/- for the same.

3. Petitioners alleged that deceased was 27 yeas of age as on the date of accident and prior to the accident, he was hale and healthy and he was working as employee at Private Bank and was he was football coach and he was earning Rs.1,80,000/- per month and he was the only earning member for their family.

They alleged accident was occurred due to the rash and negligent act of the driver of the offending vehicle and the Jurisdictional police have registered the case against the driver of the aforesaid offending vehicle in Cr.No.19/2024.

Petitioners alleged that the respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle and he has insured his vehicle with the respondent No.1, accordingly they are jointly liable to pay the compensation amount to the petitioners and they prays this tribunal to award the compensation amount with interest by allowing the petition.
4. After filing of the petition, notice served to the respondents, Respondent no.2 has not chosen to appear before this tribunal and he placed exparte.
Respondent No.1 appeared through its counsel filed vakalath and written statement by denying the entire version of the petition in toto.
Respondent No.1 has specifically denied the age, income of the deceased.
Respondent No.1 contended that insured has violated the policy conditions and accident occurred due to the negligent act of the deceased and prays this tribunal to dismiss the petition.

5. In order to prove the case, the Petitioner No.1 examined himself as PW-1 and examined two witnesses as PW-2 & 3 produced and marked 37 documents which are at Ex.P1 to 37 and they are fully cross examined.

6. Respondent No.1 has examined its official as RW-1 and examined the driver of the Lorry as RW-2,
and produced and marked 2 documents which are Ex.R1 & 2 and he is fully cross examined.
7.
I have heard the arguments form the counsel appearing for the petitioners.
Respondents are not ready to canvass their arguments orally and they are permitted to file the written arguments on merits.

On the basis of pleadings, I have framed the following:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioners prove that on 21.01.2024 at about 02.30 AM., Dasari Monish.K was moving in motor cycle bearing No.KA-03-JQ-2422, near B Channasandra skywalk, Ramamurthynagar, ring road, Bangalore, wherein the driver of the Lorry bearing Reg No.KA-53-D-6152 drove it, with high speed rash and negligent manner dashed against deceased vehicle.

Due to the impact, deceased was fell down, lorry wheel ran over the deceased and died due to the accidental injuries on the same in the hospital as alleged in the petition?
2.
Whether respondent No.1 proves that the driver of the offending vehicle was having no valid driving license, as on the date of accident as contended in the written statement ?

3. Whether the Petitioners are entitled for compensation? If so, to what amount and from whom?
4. What order or award?

9. After carefully going through the evidence placed on record and taking into consideration of facts and attending circumstances of the case, my findings to the above issues are as follows;
 Issue No.1: In the affirmative,
 Issue no.2: In the negative  issue No.3: In partly affirmative,
 Issue No.4: As per final order  for the following:
 REASONS 10. Issues no.1 to 3 :- i have taken both the issues together for common discussion, so as to avoid the repetition of facts and reasoning.
PW.1 being the petitioner no.1 and the father of the Late Monish.K, he reiterated the petition averments in his examination-in-chief affidavit.
11. According to the petitioners, the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.

In order to prove the actionable negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle, Petitioners have tendered the FIR, complaint, police intimation, mahazar, sketch,
IMV report, inquest report, PM report, final report, FSL report, which are at Ex.P1 to 11 & 14.
12.

On perusal of the aforesaid undisputed documents it is evident that Mounish died in the motor vehicle road accident caused by the negligent act of the driver of the offending vehicle that is Manjunatha Doddamani S/o Ningappa Dodamani.

Further Ex.P13 is the reply notice given by Krishna Murthy vs Oriental Insurance Co Ltd on 4 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/174265143/
3 respondent No.2, wherein he admit that Manjunatha Doddamani is the driver of the offending vehicle and he is having valid driving license and the insurance policy of his vehicle was valid as on the date of the accident.

Mahazar, IMV report, FSL report, reply notice given by respondent No.2,
final report establishes the involvement of the offending vehicle and the negligent act of the driver of the offending vehicle.
In the cross examination of PW-1 he deposed that he came to know the details of the offending vehicle in media and his son has not addicted to alcohol.
He deposed that he is a B.com graduate, and he was working in NAT West group bank and was earning Rs.33,658/-.
Further deposed that he was working as a football coach in eagle club and thereby he was earning Rs.18,000/- from the said club.

He clearly deposed that he was giving coaching from 06.00 AM to 08.00 PM., P W-2 being the employee of Nat West group, he deposed that Mounish.K was the permanent employee from 2021 and he was drawing monthly salary of Rs.37,000/-.
13. Ex
. P15, 29 are the copies of appointment letter, Ex.P.16 and 13 are the pay slips, Ex.P.17 is the bank statement.
The entry in the aforesaid documents corroborates with the oral testimony of PW-1 and 2.
Ex.P.18 to 21 are the documents / certificates given by the foot ball club, Ex.P.27 are the certificates related to Monish.K.
The aforesaid documents establishes that Monish.K was a foot ball player and he was a coach.
The aforesaid evidence establishes the income of the deceased as alleged in the petition.

14. PW-3 is the IO of the case, he has tendered the statement given by the eye witnesses that is Preyanch Kumar and Devu Yadav as per Ex.P.33 and 34 and he deposed that he came to know about the details of the offending vehicle through the aforesaid witness.
He has tendered copy of request given to RTO to give the IMV report of the vehicles involved in the accident as per Ex.P.35, and IMV report are at Ex.P.7 & 8.
He has tendered request given to the FSL authority to conduct the luminal test as per Ex.P.36 and FSL report is at Ex.P.32.
He deposed that there is no CC camera near the metro working place.
The aforesaid material facts are elicited by respondent No.1 in the cross examination of PW-2.
The oral testimony of PW-2 corroborates with the investigation reports.

Nothing worth is elicited to disprove the investigation and the evidence gathered by the IO, so far as the alleged incident and the negligent act of the driver of the offending vehicle is concerned which resulting in the death of Monish.

15. Ex.P14 is the FSL report, it reveals that Monish had not consumed the alcohol, Ex.P.32 is the FSL report it reveals that blood stains are found on the back left side wheels joint and the said samples corroborates with the blood sample of the deceased.
The aforesaid undisputed evidence fortifies the version of the petitioners.
RW-2 is the driver of the offending vehicle in his examination-in-chief, he admit that criminal case filed against him is pending for adjudication.
In his cross examination he admitted that final report is filed against him as per Ex.P.11 and he has secured the bail from the competent court.
16. Respondent No.1 has failed to probabilise the fact that accident occurred due to the negligent act of the deceased.
Further more, there is no allegation against the deceased in the final report.

sentences.text: There is no material on record to disbelieve the petitioner version.
17. Petitioners have examined employee of NAT West group as PW-2, his oral testimony corroborate with employment letter and pay slips related to the deceased.
As per the pay slip for the month December 2023 the gross salary of the deceased was Rs.36,408/-.

Ex.P18 is the offer letter given by Avishkaar sports, Ex.P20, 21 is the contract letter issued from Bengaluru Eagle foot ball club, and it further reveals that monthly Rs.20,000/- was given to the Monish for his services.
In the cross examination of PW-1, the aforesaid facts elicited by the respondent No.1 accordingly, in total Monish was having monthly income of Rs.74,404/-.
As per Income tax new slab regime for the financial year 2023-24, Monish has to pay monthly income tax of Rs.3,505/- including the 4% cess and professional tax.
Accordingly the income of the Monish is assessed as Rs.70,903/-.
18. Further more as per the entry in Aadhar card of the deceased which is Ex.P.24, the date of birth of the deceased is 28.04.1996.
Accordingly the age of the deceased as on the date of the accident was 27 years, 8 months and 23 days and multiplier 17 is applicable.
19. Deceased was self employee, salaried person and unmarried and he was below 40 years,
accordingly 50% should be added towards his monthly income for future prospectus.
Deceased was unmarried accordingly 1/2 should be deducted from his monthly income towards his personal expenses.

20. The loss of dependency is calculated as follows:
1 Monthly income Rs. 70,903/-
Add: 50% of income future prospectus Rs. 35,451/-

Monthly income Rs. 1,06,354/-
2 Less; 1/2 for personal expenses Rs. 53,117/-
4 Monthly income Rs. 53,117/-
 Rs.53,117 (income)X 12 (month) X 17 Rs.1,08,35,868/-
 (Multiplier )
 Accordingly petitioners are entitled for Rs.1,08,35,868/- as compensation under the head Loss of Dependency.
21. Loss of estate;
As per the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Pranaya sethi case, Tribunal has to award Rs.15,000/- as compensation under this head.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Magma GIC V/s Nanuram case, wherein the concept of consortium is categorically discussed.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, in Sarala Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport corporation reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121, wherein it is held that it is just and proper to award interest at the rate of 6% p.a.
